name: Bidirectional inverter-charger
summary: A battery converter that charges from an AC source and inverts back to AC, with an internal transfer relay for the load.
description: An inverter-charger contains one bidirectional power stage between a battery and an AC output, together with an internal transfer relay connecting the AC input to the output when a valid source is present. With the source available it passes power through and charges the battery; without it, it opens the relay and inverts from the battery.

Drawings show a converter box with DC and AC marks, a bidirectional arrow, an AC input from the grid or generator and an AC output to the load. The transfer relay may be drawn inside the boundary as a changeover contact, and some units have a second output that drops during battery operation.

The symbol does not show the internal neutral-earth relay many units use when inverting, which matters for earthing and residual current device operation. Power assist settings, which let the inverter add battery power to a limited generator supply, are also invisible on the drawing.
readingNotes: Look for the internal transfer relay and any neutral-earth relay.
Check whether a second output is shed on battery operation.
drawingChecklist: State inverter VA, charger current and battery voltage.
Show AC input, outputs and earthing arrangement.
distinction: An inverter-charger has an internal transfer relay and charger; a plain DC-to-AC inverter only converts battery power to AC.
